stories.headline: East Cambridgeshire cottage to be replaced by flats
stories.brief: A cottage in East Cambridgeshire is set to be demolished. Planning permission has been granted for the site to be redeveloped, with the existing property being replaced by a block of flats.

stories.headline: Long-term future secured for Long Sutton Market House
stories.brief: Lincolnshire County Council has announced that the long-term future of the Market House in Long Sutton has been secured. The local authority confirmed the news regarding the historic site, though further details on the specific plans for the building have not yet been released. Residents and those interested in the future of the town’s landmarks are advised to keep an eye on official council updates for more information as it becomes available.

stories.headline: Police appeal for missing woman
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire police have expressed growing concern for a woman who has been reported missing. Officers say she failed to return home as expected, prompting an appeal for information. Authorities are urging anyone who may have seen her or who has knowledge of her current whereabouts to come forward to assist with their enquiries.

stories.headline: Wisbech cinema to screen capybara documentary this Sunday
stories.brief: A new documentary exploring the global popularity of the capybara is coming to The Light cinema in Wisbech this Sunday. Titled "The Route to Cappyness," the 99-minute film examines how the rodent became an internet icon and a symbol of calm. Directed by Sharon Walia, the production features footage filmed across Brazil, Japan, the United States, and the UK. The documentary is rated U and is scheduled to begin at 5.35pm.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn man charged with public order offences
stories.brief:
A 48-year-old man from South Lynn is due to appear in court next month following his arrest on Saddlebow Road. James Evans, of Saddlebow Road, has been charged with two counts of public order offences. The charges relate to an alleged incident on September 21 at a public building on Chapel Street, as well as a further incident during his arrest yesterday.

Mr Evans was taken to the King’s Lynn Police Investigation Centre for questioning before being released on bail. He is scheduled to appear at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on November 5.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire resident targeted in attempted phone scam
stories.brief: A woman from Cambridgeshire has reported an attempted scam after receiving a phone call from someone claiming to be the Pope. The caller requested a payment of £500. The incident, reported by the Ely Standard, highlights a recent attempt to defraud a local resident. Authorities continue to advise the public to remain vigilant against unexpected requests for money over the telephone.

stories.headline: Two men convicted of hare coursing in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Two men have been found guilty of attending a hare coursing event. The conviction was confirmed by Cambridgeshire Constabulary. No further details regarding the location or the sentencing of the individuals have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Admissions remain suspended at King’s Lynn mental health ward
stories.brief:
Admissions to the Samphire Ward at Chatterton House in King’s Lynn remain temporarily paused. The Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust says the suspension is based on quality and safety grounds and will continue for the coming months. No date has been set for the ward to reopen to new patients.

The trust confirms that Chatterton House remains open, and anyone requiring inpatient care will be offered a bed elsewhere within the organisation. The pause is part of a wider transformation programme for mental health services across the region, which includes plans for a new neighbourhood mental health centre in King’s Lynn. Officials state that patient and staff safety remains their highest priority while this work is completed.

stories.headline: Changes to Peterborough coaching staff
stories.brief: Peterborough United have confirmed that coaching staff members Ryan Harley and Connell Rawlinson have left the club. The departures were announced following reports from the BBC. No further details regarding the reasons for their exit or potential replacements have been provided by the club at this time.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over road maintenance funding in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A report from the Ely Standard suggests that East Cambridgeshire is receiving an unfair share of the budget allocated for road maintenance across the county. The publication claims the district is getting a raw deal regarding how these funds are distributed. Local officials and residents have expressed concerns about the current system used to determine how money is split between different areas. There has been no official response yet regarding a potential review of the allocation process.

stories.headline: Police appeal for missing woman
stories.brief:
Cambridgeshire Police have issued an appeal for a woman who has been reported missing. Officers say they are becoming increasingly concerned for her welfare after she failed to return home. 

Authorities are urging anyone with information regarding her whereabouts to come forward. Further details are expected to be released as the search continues.

stories.headline: Overnight roadworks planned for Hardwick Roundabout
stories.brief:
Motorists in King’s Lynn are being warned of upcoming disruption as survey work begins at the Hardwick Roundabout. Starting Monday, October 12, Norfolk County Council will implement overnight lane closures and traffic light controls on sections of the A47 and A10. These measures are scheduled between 8pm and 6am to minimise impact on daytime traffic.

The surveys are part of the West Winch Housing Access Road project and are expected to last until the end of November, though some work may extend into early December. Contractors will be assessing road surfaces and drainage. While the majority of the project is scheduled for overnight, officials have confirmed that any particularly noisy tasks will be completed before 11pm.

stories.headline: Family pays tribute to man found dead in Peterborough
stories.brief: The family of a man discovered dead in Peterborough have released a public tribute. Relatives have described the individual as a "lovely dad." No further details regarding the circumstances of the death or the identity of the man have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire County Council launches public spending survey
stories.brief:
People living across Cambridgeshire are being invited to share their views on how the local council should allocate its budget. A new survey has been launched to help officials understand the spending priorities of residents across the region. 

The local authority is encouraging members of the public to take part in the consultation process to help shape future financial decisions. Further details on how to participate in the survey can be found on the official Cambridgeshire County Council website.

stories.headline: Further evidence required regarding former brickworks site
stories.brief: Officials have stated that more information is needed to address ongoing concerns surrounding a former brickworks site. The update, reported by the BBC, suggests that current evidence is insufficient to resolve the issues raised about the location. No further details regarding the nature of the concerns or the specific site have been provided at this time. Residents are advised that the matter remains under review as authorities seek additional clarity.

stories.headline: Looking back at October 2013 business news in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
We are taking a look back at business stories from October 2013 across the region. During that month, the Fenman pub, located opposite the King’s Lynn railway station, reopened its doors following a £15,000 refurbishment. The project was led by owners Tony and Julie Thompson.

Elsewhere in the area, Beers of Europe in Garage Lane, Setchey, received planning permission to expand their site. The approval was granted despite some concerns raised regarding road safety. These stories formed part of the local business landscape in the Fens ten years ago.

stories.headline: East Cambridgeshire approves new inclusive playground strategy
stories.brief: East Cambridgeshire District Council has officially approved a new strategy aimed at increasing the number of inclusive playgrounds across the region. The plan focuses on creating play areas that are accessible to all children, ensuring facilities meet a wider range of needs. Local families can expect to see these improvements implemented as the council begins to roll out the new policy. Further details regarding specific locations and timelines for these upgrades are expected to be released as the project progresses.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn charity event helps tackle veteran isolation
stories.brief:
A King’s Lynn charity has hosted a social evening to help combat isolation among the local Armed Forces community. Beneficiaries of The Bridge for Heroes enjoyed a trip to the Strikes bowling alley in Gaywood, followed by a fish and chip supper at the charity’s South Clough Lane centre. 

The outing was made possible through funding from Project Out and About Norfolk, which is supported by the Norfolk Community Foundation. The initiative aims to improve mental health by providing activities for veterans and their families across West Norfolk. Members of the Armed Forces community interested in learning more about these services can contact The Bridge for Heroes on 01553 760230.

stories.headline: Firefighters tackle field blaze in Fenland
stories.brief: Fire crews are currently responding to a field fire in a Fenland town. Emergency services were called to the scene to manage the blaze. No further details regarding the exact location or the cause of the fire have been released at this time. Residents are advised to stay clear of the area while operations continue.

stories.headline: Ethical coffee chain set to open in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
A new organic coffee shop is coming to King’s Lynn. Esquires, The Organic Coffee Company, is planning to move into the former Coneys, Burton, and Dorothy Perkins premises at 98 to 99 High Street. The site has remained vacant since February, but workmen have been spotted inside the building this week. 

West Norfolk Council has granted planning permission for the chain to install its signage at the location. The application was submitted by brand project manager Ash Flawn. Esquires, which originated in Canada, recently opened another franchise in Swaffham. The company has not yet confirmed an official opening date for the new King’s Lynn branch.

stories.headline: Peterborough man faces court over indecent images charge
stories.brief: A man from Peterborough has appeared in court accused of encouraging a young boy to share nude photographs. The case was heard following reports published by the BBC. No further details regarding the defendant or the specific court proceedings have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Long Sutton housing development plans refused
stories.brief: Plans for a new housing development in Long Sutton have been turned down by the local council. The proposal sought permission to build more than 120 homes in the area. South Holland District Council has rejected the application, meaning the project will not proceed as planned.

stories.headline: Planning decision for Brewin Avenue to go to committee
stories.brief: A planning application for Brewin Avenue in March is set to be decided by a committee. This follows objections from both local planning officers and the town of March, who have both advised against the proposal. Despite these recommendations, the application will now be reviewed by the Fenland District Council planning committee for a final decision.

stories.headline: Woman hospitalised following Wisbech collision
stories.brief:
Emergency services were called to Clarkson Avenue in Wisbech yesterday afternoon following a two-vehicle crash. Police and paramedics arrived at the scene at 2:23pm to assist those involved. 

One woman was taken to hospital to be treated for minor injuries. The vehicles have since been recovered from the site, and the road has been reopened to traffic.

stories.headline: Plans submitted to replace former King’s Lynn clinic with new homes
stories.brief:
Developers Alan Homes have submitted a planning application to demolish the former King’s Lynn Chiropractic Centre on John Kennedy Road. The Downham Market-based firm is seeking permission to build seven two-bedroom houses on the site. 

The proposal follows an earlier, larger plan for nine homes which was scaled back following concerns regarding noise and the impact on neighbouring properties. If approved, the new two-storey dwellings will include private garden space and features designed to mitigate flood risk. The application was submitted to West Norfolk Council this week, with a final decision expected by the first of December.

stories.headline: Police investigate assault in Fenland town
stories.brief: A man has been taken to hospital following an assault in a Fenland town. Details regarding the exact location and the time of the incident have not been released by authorities. Police are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the attack. Anyone with information that could assist officers with their enquiries is encouraged to come forward.

stories.headline: Fenland District Council submits formal objection to Leverington housing plans
stories.brief:
Fenland District Council has submitted a detailed formal objection to the Home Office regarding plans to house 26 women and babies at Roman Court in Leverington. The council argues the site lacks the necessary facilities and services to support asylum seekers, warning that the proposal poses risks to both residents and those being housed. 

The local authority is also challenging a wider government proposal to accommodate 205 asylum seekers across the district, describing that figure as unreasonable. Officials have requested that the Home Office reconsider the plan, noting that the council has not been properly consulted. The Home Office has confirmed it will review the council's submission before reaching a final decision on the site.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn firewalk raises funds for local charities
stories.brief:
Participants have taken part in a charity firewalk at Lynnsport in King’s Lynn. The event, held last Friday, was organised by the King’s Lynn Priory Satellite Rotary Club. Six teams and five individuals walked barefoot across hot coals to raise money for eight different Norfolk charities. 

The challenge was led by Mark and Tanya Daniels from Charity Firewalk, who also provided a fire performance for those in attendance. While the final total raised is not yet known, organisers have thanked the various sponsors and volunteers who supported the event. Last year’s inaugural firewalk raised more than £33,000. Donations are still being collected to support the chosen local causes.

stories.headline: Questions raised over town hall sale
stories.brief: A local councillor is seeking answers regarding the recent sale of a town hall to a businessman. The transaction has been defended by officials following the request for further information. No further details regarding the location or the identity of those involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police appeal for witnesses following fatal Sawtry collision
stories.brief:
A 23-year-old motorcyclist from Yaxley has died following a collision in Sawtry earlier this week. The incident occurred on Old North Road at approximately 12:50pm, involving a black Kawasaki motorbike and a red Volvo lorry. The motorcyclist was taken to Addenbrooke’s Hospital but later passed away from his injuries.

The 76-year-old lorry driver from Wisbech was uninjured. He was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by careless driving and has been released on bail until January 4. Police are asking anyone with dashcam footage or information regarding the incident to come forward. You can report details via the force website quoting reference 35/77423/26, or by calling 101.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn hospital team to tackle 10K obstacle course for charity
stories.brief:
A team of therapists from the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn is preparing to take on a 10K inflatable obstacle course on Saturday, October 17. The group, consisting of occupational therapists and physiotherapists, will be dressed as characters from the Toy Story films to raise money for the children’s therapy department.

The team aims to reach a £2,500 target to purchase specialist equipment, toys, and resources to support young patients with physical and developmental needs. So far, they have raised over £230. Supporters can contribute to the cause via the team’s JustGiving page, which is linked on the hospital’s social media channels.

stories.headline: Plans announced for 32 domestic abuse refuge spaces
stories.brief: New proposals have been put forward to secure 32 refuge spaces for victims of domestic abuse. The plans aim to increase the availability of safe accommodation for those in need of support. Further details regarding the location and implementation of these spaces have not yet been confirmed.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn singer progresses on The Voice UK
stories.brief: A singer from King’s Lynn has successfully reached the battle rounds of The Voice UK. Adam Tucker performed the Robbie Williams hit ‘Feel’ during the show’s blind auditions, which aired on ITV over the weekend. His performance prompted coaches Danny Jones and Tom Fletcher to turn their chairs, securing him the final spot on their team. Mr. Tucker, who provided the singing voice for Robbie Williams in the 2024 biopic Better Man, said he is now ready to step out of the shadows and establish his own identity as an artist. He will next appear on the programme on Saturday, October 17, as he competes for a place in the semi-finals.

stories.headline: Emergency services attend incident at Queensgate Bus Station
stories.brief: Emergency services have been called to Queensgate Bus Station in Peterborough following reports of a sudden death. Authorities were dispatched to the scene to respond to the incident. No further details regarding the circumstances have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Emergency services respond to three-vehicle crash in Ely
stories.brief: Emergency crews have been called to the scene of a road traffic collision in Ely. The incident involves three vehicles. Local authorities are currently managing the situation, and updates are expected as the response continues. Motorists in the area are advised to remain alert for potential travel disruption while emergency teams carry out their work.

stories.headline: Teenager sentenced for assault in Spalding
stories.brief: A teenager has avoided a prison sentence following an attack on a transgender woman in Spalding. The case, reported by the Spalding South Holland News, concluded with the court opting against custody for the offender. No further details regarding the sentencing conditions or the identity of those involved have been released.

stories.headline: Plans for new King’s Lynn supermarket and drive-thru units rejected
stories.brief:
Proposals for a new Lidl supermarket and two drive-thru units at Morston Point in King’s Lynn have been turned down by West Norfolk Council. The development, which promised to create 90 jobs, was rejected on Monday due to concerns over highway safety and a lack of commitment to local infrastructure improvements. 

Planning officers cited potential flood risks and inadequate landscaping as reasons for the refusal. Officials also raised concerns regarding the lack of public transport and cycle facilities, warning that the site could cause conflict between road users. Meanwhile, separate plans for a nearby retail development on land south of Beveridge Way remain open for public consultation until October 12.

stories.headline: Police appeal following quad bike theft
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police are appealing for information after a quad bike was stolen in the area. Officers are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the theft and are asking anyone who may have witnessed suspicious activity or has relevant information to come forward. You can contact the police directly to assist with their ongoing enquiries.

stories.headline: Anglian Water prosecuted following Whittlesey pollution incident
stories.brief: Anglian Water has faced prosecution following a pollution incident in Whittlesey. The event resulted in the deaths of up to 1,000 fish. No further details regarding the cause or the legal outcome have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Queen Elizabeth Hospital marks Baby Loss Awareness Week
stories.brief:
The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn is inviting the public to participate in remembrance activities during Baby Loss Awareness Week, running from Friday, October 9 to Thursday, October 15. Visitors are encouraged to tie ribbons in the hospital’s Butterfly Garden as a sign of unity. Ribbons can be brought from home or collected at the main reception.

A memorial service, themed around stars, will be held in the hospital’s Sacred Space on Sunday, October 12, at 3pm. Additionally, the Arthur Levin Day Surgery Unit will be illuminated in blue and pink at 7pm on October 15 for the annual Wave of Light, where members of the community are invited to light candles in support.

stories.headline: Peterborough manager calls for mentality shift
stories.brief: Peterborough manager Robbie Savage has publicly called for a change in mentality from his squad. The boss is looking for a shift in approach from his players following recent performances. No further details regarding specific changes or upcoming fixtures have been confirmed at this stage.

stories.headline: Plans proposed for new school in disused building
stories.brief: A vacant property could be transformed into a new school. According to reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, proposals have been put forward to repurpose the disused building for educational use. No further details regarding the location or the timeline for the project have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Report identifies village as one of the country's most deprived areas
stories.brief: A report from the Lynn News has highlighted a local village as one of the most deprived areas in the country. The publication describes the location as the "most forgotten" village, drawing attention to its current socio-economic status. No further details regarding the specific identity of the village or the criteria used for the assessment were provided in the report. Residents are encouraged to stay tuned to Fenland Angels Radio for any further updates on this story as they become available.

stories.headline: Three arrested following reports of youths with a knife in Fen town
stories.brief: Police have made three arrests after reports of a group of youths carrying a knife in a Fenland town. Among those taken into custody is a boy. Officers were called to the scene following the reports, leading to the arrests of the three individuals. Investigations into the incident are currently ongoing.

stories.headline: Queen Elizabeth Hospital staff honoured at annual awards
stories.brief:
Staff at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn have been recognised for their dedication and innovation at the annual Team QEH Awards. More than 300 guests gathered at the Corn Exchange to celebrate the achievements of hospital employees and volunteers. 

Over 400 nominations were submitted by patients and colleagues, resulting in 14 awards being presented across various categories. The evening highlighted contributions ranging from clinical care and research to maintenance and volunteer support. The final honour of the night, the Special Recognition Award, was presented to Head of Midwifery Esther Dorken for her work in improving maternity services and fostering teamwork within her division.

stories.headline: Fire crews tackle field blaze in Fenland
stories.brief: Firefighters are currently responding to a field fire in a Fenland town. Emergency crews are on the scene working to bring the blaze under control. Residents are advised to be aware of potential disruption in the area while operations continue. Further updates will be provided as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: New supported housing project opens for women in South Lynn
stories.brief:
A new housing project for women transitioning from homelessness has opened in South Lynn. The Purfleet Trust has partnered with Hughes Electrical and content creator Hayley Rubery to renovate a three-bedroom property. Hughes Electrical donated essential appliances, including a cooker, fridge, and washing machine, while Miss Rubery led the interior design to create a welcoming environment.

The house is part of the charity’s Training House project, which provides shared accommodation for up to three residents. Women living there will receive support with life skills such as budgeting and tenancy management. The Purfleet Trust, based at Austin Fields, supports over 1,000 people across West Norfolk annually through various homelessness prevention and wellbeing services.

stories.headline: Peterborough United Under-21s defeat Ipswich Town
stories.brief: Peterborough United’s Under-21 side secured a victory against Ipswich Town in their latest fixture. The match concluded with a final score of 4-1 in favour of Peterborough United.

stories.headline: Plans to secure 32 domestic abuse refuge spaces
stories.brief: New proposals have been announced to provide 32 dedicated spaces for domestic abuse victims. The initiative aims to secure refuge accommodation for those in need of support. Further details regarding the location and implementation of these spaces are expected to follow as the plans progress.

stories.headline: Man arrested following knife incident in Spalding
stories.brief: Police have arrested a man following reports that people were threatened with a knife in Spalding town centre. Officers were called to the scene to deal with the incident. An investigation into the matter is currently underway.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire woman wins £1 million lottery prize
stories.brief: A mother from Cambridgeshire has secured a £1 million windfall after winning the lottery. The win comes just two weeks after she played a prank on her partner involving a scratchcard. Details regarding the specific lottery game or the winner's identity have not been released.

stories.headline: Gas pipe upgrade work begins in Wisbech
stories.brief:
Engineers from Cadent have begun a project to upgrade over 400 metres of gas piping across several streets in Wisbech, including Norwich Road, Churchill Road, and King Street. The work, which aims to future-proof the local network, is scheduled for completion by Friday, December 18. 

Drivers should expect various traffic management measures, including rolling closures on Norwich Road and lane restrictions on Churchill Road. While gas supplies will remain on for most, some properties may experience short, temporary disconnections. Residents are reminded to contact the National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999 if they smell gas. Cambridgeshire County Council has confirmed that the road surfaces affected by these works were intentionally left pending resurfacing.

stories.headline: Series of drink-driving convictions at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
stories.brief:
King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court dealt with a high volume of motoring offences last week, with several drivers disqualified for being over the alcohol limit. Among those sentenced were Anthony Purdy, who received a 40-month ban after crashing a van into railings in Gaywood, and Claire Pannell, who was disqualified for 23 months following an incident on the A17.

In other cases, a Wisbech man, Andrew Mawer, appeared on serious charges and has been sent to Norwich Crown Court. Additionally, a warrant was issued for the arrest of Shelby Sands after she failed to appear in court, while Danny Wilson was ordered to pay compensation for damaging his mother’s property.

stories.headline: Appeal for witnesses following serious collision in Sawtry
stories.brief:
Police are appealing for information after a serious collision between a lorry and a motorbike in Sawtry yesterday afternoon. The incident occurred at approximately 12:50pm on the B1043 Old North Road, involving a red Volvo HGV and a black Kawasaki motorcycle. The 23-year-old rider from Yaxley was taken to Addenbrooke’s Hospital with life-threatening injuries. 

The 76-year-old lorry driver from Wisbech was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by careless driving and has been released on bail until January 4. Officers are urging anyone who witnessed the collision or has relevant dashcam footage to contact the police via their website or by calling 101, quoting reference 35/77423/26.

stories.headline: NHS supply lorry drivers announce strike action
stories.brief:
Lorry drivers responsible for delivering essential NHS supplies, including those to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn, are set to take industrial action. Nearly 200 drivers employed by GXO have voted to strike after rejecting a four per cent pay offer. The walkouts are scheduled for several dates between October 13 and November 12.

The Unite union claims the workers face inferior terms compared to standard NHS contracts. While the union warns that action could intensify if the dispute remains unresolved, an NHS Supply Chain spokesperson stated that GXO has contingency plans in place to help minimise any potential disruption to hospital supplies.

stories.headline: Investment boost for Ely housing and Mepal solar energy
stories.brief: A new investment of £778,000 has been announced for projects across East Cambridgeshire. The funding is set to support the development of affordable housing within the city of Ely. Additionally, the capital will be used to install solar power infrastructure in the village of Mepal. The investment aims to address local housing needs while also supporting renewable energy initiatives in the region.

stories.headline: Parent supports student protest following school suspension
stories.brief: A parent has publicly backed their son’s decision to protest at school, despite the student being suspended as a result of his actions. The parent stated they support the child's right to demonstrate. No further details regarding the school involved or the nature of the protest have been released at this time.

stories.headline: NHS bosses deny further cuts to Doddington and Wisbech hospitals
stories.brief:
Health officials have confirmed there are no plans to permanently close or reduce services at hospitals in Doddington and Wisbech. Representatives from the Queen Elizabeth Hospital and North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trusts addressed concerns regarding recent service changes at a Cambridgeshire County Council committee meeting. 

While endoscopy services were moved from Wisbech to King’s Lynn for patient safety, and several clinics at Doddington were suspended due to staffing, officials described these as temporary measures. They rejected claims of neglect, stating that services are being relocated rather than cut. However, local councillors highlighted that transport barriers make it difficult for Fenland residents to reach alternative sites, arguing that reduced local access effectively functions as a service cut.

stories.headline: Bridge Road closed in Sutton Bridge following collision
stories.brief:
Drivers in Sutton Bridge are being advised to avoid Bridge Road this afternoon following a road traffic collision. Lincolnshire Police are currently at the scene near the junction with Allenby’s Chase. 

The incident is causing knock-on delays for traffic travelling along the nearby A17. Motorists are encouraged to seek alternative routes while emergency services manage the situation.

stories.headline: Police investigation continues following Wisbech murder
stories.brief:
Police inquiries are ongoing into the death of 37-year-old Atis Bleive in Wisbech. Officers were called to a property on Osborne Road at approximately 4pm on January 19, where Mr Bleive was pronounced dead at the scene. A post-mortem examination confirmed he died from a stab wound to the abdomen.

Two local people were arrested on suspicion of murder. A 41-year-old man was released under investigation, while a 45-year-old woman remains on bail until December 29. Detectives have confirmed that the investigation into the incident is continuing.

stories.headline: Hunstanton fundraiser hits £30,000 milestone for Queen Elizabeth Hospital
stories.brief: A Hunstanton woman has reached a fundraising milestone of £30,000 for the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. Maggie Drew has spent over four years raising money in memory of her mother, Moira, who passed away in July 2020. Her efforts have included hosting music nights, bake sales, and supermarket collections. The funds have supported various hospital departments, including the stroke unit, where they helped purchase specialist wheelchairs. Ms. Drew was recently named a finalist in the Local Hero Awards for her work. Hospital staff have praised her dedication, noting that the contributions help provide care beyond what standard NHS funding allows. Those interested in supporting the hospital charity can find more information at qehklcharity.co.uk.

stories.headline: Government approves Peterborough SEND reform plan
stories.brief: The government has officially approved a new reform plan for Special Educational Needs and Disabilities services in Peterborough. The proposal aims to improve the support provided to children and young people across the area. Local families and those involved in the education sector are expected to see changes as the council begins implementing the government-backed strategy. Further details regarding the timeline and specific service adjustments are expected to follow as the local authority moves forward with the approved reforms.

stories.headline: Van fire causes road closure in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A busy road in East Cambridgeshire has been closed following a van fire. Emergency services were called to the scene to deal with the blaze, which has resulted in the route being shut to traffic. Motorists travelling through the area are advised to expect delays and seek alternative routes while the incident is managed. No further details regarding the cause of the fire or any potential injuries have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police investigate theft in Long Sutton
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police are investigating an incident in Long Sutton where a woman allegedly posed as a carer to steal money from an elderly man. Authorities are looking into the circumstances surrounding the theft. Residents are reminded to remain vigilant when answering the door to unexpected visitors and to always verify the identity of anyone claiming to be a professional carer. Anyone with information regarding this incident is encouraged to contact the police.

stories.headline: Update on Whittlesey leisure centre plans
stories.brief: There has been a major update regarding the proposed eighteen point seven million pound leisure centre in Whittlesey. Further details on the development plans have been released following reports from the March Chatteris Whittlesey News. Residents are advised to keep an eye on local updates as the project progresses.

stories.headline: Wisbech man prosecuted for fly-tipping offences
stories.brief:
A 44-year-old man from Wisbech has been fined £680 following four incidents of fly-tipping in Chestnut Road. The offences occurred between June and August 2025. Fenland District Council brought the prosecution after the individual failed to pay an initial fixed penalty notice. Peterborough Magistrates Court ordered the fine, which includes prosecution costs and a victim surcharge, to be deducted from the man’s Universal Credit payments.

Fenland District Council is reminding residents of their legal responsibility to dispose of waste correctly. Officials warn that both those who dump rubbish and householders who fail to ensure their waste is handled by responsible carriers can face legal action or financial penalties.

stories.headline: New sustainable housing development underway in Gaywood
stories.brief:
West Norfolk councillors have visited the Florence Fields development in Gaywood to inspect progress on the new sustainable housing project. The site, which is expected to be fully complete by late 2027, will provide 226 homes in total. Officials confirmed that over 40 per cent of these properties are designated for private and affordable rent, supported by a six-million-pound government grant.

The development features eco-friendly heating, electric vehicle charging points, and solar panels. Plans also include over eight acres of open space and improvements to a nearby play area. Council leaders noted that 62 homes are already occupied, with the project also providing local employment and apprenticeship opportunities throughout the construction process.

stories.headline: Questions raised over £3.9 million Cambridgeshire Horizons funding
stories.brief: Local authorities in Fenland, Huntingdonshire, and East Cambridgeshire are facing questions regarding the use of a £3.9 million windfall. The funding was originally provided to the three councils by Cambridgeshire Horizons. Reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News are now examining how this significant sum of money has been spent by the local government bodies. Residents across the region are being encouraged to look into the details of the allocation as the investigation into the distribution of these funds continues.

stories.headline: Peterborough United manager receives fitness boost
stories.brief: The new manager of Peterborough United has been handed an early fitness boost for his squad. Meanwhile, an update has been issued regarding the club's international players. Further details on the team's preparations are expected as the season progresses.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire child sex offender jailed following DNA match
stories.brief: A child sex offender from Cambridgeshire has been sentenced to time in prison. The conviction was secured after a DNA match linked the individual to the crimes. No further details regarding the identity of the offender or the specific location of the offences have been released at this time.

stories.headline: New eye screening service launched by Moorfields Private
stories.brief: Moorfields Private has introduced a new eye screening service. The announcement was reported by LaingBuisson News. No further details regarding the location or availability of this service have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Red Arrows spotted over Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: The Red Arrows have been seen flying over Cambridgeshire. According to reports from the Ely Standard, photographs and video footage have captured the Royal Air Force aerobatic team soaring across the local skies.

stories.headline: Optometrists identify signs of atrial fibrillation in the eye
stories.brief: The Association of Optometrists has reported that indicators of atrial fibrillation can be detected through eye examinations. The professional body highlights that these findings may assist in identifying the heart condition during routine sight tests. Residents across the Fens are advised that this development links ocular health assessments to the early detection of heart rhythm irregularities. Further information regarding these clinical findings is available through the Association of Optometrists.

stories.headline: East Cambridgeshire pensioners encouraged to check benefit eligibility
stories.brief: Residents in East Cambridgeshire are being urged to check if they are eligible for Pension Credit. Officials suggest that those who qualify could receive financial support worth up to £4,300 per year. Local households are being encouraged to review their circumstances to ensure they are not missing out on this potential assistance. Further details regarding the support and how to apply can be found through official government channels.

stories.headline: Chatteris woman jailed for attempted arson
stories.brief: A woman from Chatteris has been sentenced to time in prison following an incident involving a deodorant can. The individual was convicted of attempted arson. No further details regarding the circumstances of the case or the length of the sentence have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police investigation underway in Peterborough
stories.brief: Police have launched an investigation following the discovery of a body in Peterborough. Officers are currently looking into the circumstances surrounding the death. No further details have been released by authorities at this time.

stories.headline: Government delays Cambridgeshire council reform plans
stories.brief: Plans to reform local government structures in Cambridgeshire have been put on hold. The government has confirmed a delay to the proposed changes, which were originally reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News. No new timeline for the reforms has been announced at this stage.

stories.headline: Brad Pitt stars in new film Heart of the Beast at The Light, Wisbech
stories.brief: Film fans in Wisbech can now catch the new release Heart of the Beast at The Light cinema. The film features Brad Pitt as James Belmont, a retired special forces veteran who travels to the Alaskan wilderness with his combat dog, Odin. After a mid-air medical emergency during a storm, the pair must navigate fifty miles of dangerous terrain to reach safety. The 12A-rated movie also stars JK Simmons and Anna Lambe. Critics have described the production as a mix of action and sentimentality, highlighting the performance of the lead actor. Check local listings at The Light for screening times.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn hospital specialist wins national mentoring award
stories.brief:
A health play specialist at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has been named Mentor of the Year 2026. Nicola Wright received the national honour from the charity Starlight for her work supporting apprentice Claire Burrell. The award recognises professionals who improve children’s experiences of healthcare through play. 

Ms Wright, who has worked in the field since 2005, was nominated by her apprentice for providing guidance and professional development over the past two years. The presentation took place at the hospital on Tuesday, September 29. The Starlight Health Play Awards are held in conjunction with National Play in Healthcare Week, which runs from October 5 to 9.

stories.headline: Police investigation underway in Peterborough
stories.brief: Police have launched an investigation following the discovery of a body in Peterborough. Officers are currently looking into the circumstances surrounding the death. No further details have been released by authorities at this time.

stories.headline: Ely public toilets closed following vandalism
stories.brief: Public toilets in Ely have been forced to close after being targeted by vandals. The damage, which involved the facility's pipework, resulted in significant flooding at the site. Local authorities have not yet indicated when the toilets will be reopened to the public.

stories.headline: Protests held against Leverington asylum hostel plans
stories.brief:
Residents gathered at Roman Court in Leverington on Sunday to protest government plans to convert the building into a hostel for asylum seekers. Organised by Councillor Chris Tirrell, the demonstration aimed to voice community opposition to the proposal, which could eventually house 205 people in the area. 

Fenland District Council and MP Steve Barclay have formally objected to the scheme, citing concerns over public safety and the building's condition following a previous prohibition notice regarding asbestos. A further protest is scheduled for this Sunday, October 11, at 11am at the Roman Court site. The government is expected to reach a final decision on the proposal by Friday, October 16.

stories.headline: Pizza Hut closes at King’s Lynn retail park
stories.brief:
A long-standing Pizza Hut restaurant at the Hardwick Retail Park in King’s Lynn has closed its doors for good. The site, which served customers for decades, officially ceased operations on September 26. Signage has been removed and the premises are currently vacant. A spokesperson for the company thanked staff and customers for their support, noting that the nearest alternative branch is located in Peterborough.

Meanwhile, the fried chicken chain Popeyes has begun advertising for a general manager for a new store in King’s Lynn. While the company has not yet confirmed the location or opening date for the new restaurant, the job listing offers a salary of up to £44,000.

stories.headline: Knife Angel sculpture goes on display
stories.brief: A sculpture known as the Knife Angel is currently being exhibited. The artwork has been constructed using 100,000 knives that were previously seized by authorities. The piece is now available for public viewing.

stories.headline: Peterborough United manager monitors EFL developments
stories.brief: The manager of Peterborough United has been spotted observing Huddersfield Town’s recent rise to third place in the league standings. Meanwhile, a striker currently on loan from the Posh has successfully found the back of the net. Additionally, updates have been released regarding the latest progress in the EFL Trophy.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire curry house shortlisted for national award
stories.brief: A curry house based in Cambridgeshire has been named as a contender for a prestigious national prize. The restaurant is currently in the running for the top honour, according to reports from the Ely Standard. Further details regarding the specific name of the establishment or the nature of the award have not been disclosed.

stories.headline: Live facial recognition technology deployed in Cambridge
stories.brief: Police in Cambridge have begun using live facial recognition technology. The system is designed to help officers identify wanted individuals in public spaces. The rollout follows reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News regarding the implementation of this new surveillance method within the city. Residents and visitors to the area should be aware that this technology is now in operation.

stories.headline: Court of Appeal overturns solicitor fraud ruling
stories.brief: The Court of Appeal has overturned a previous legal ruling concerning a solicitor accused of ignoring fraud. The original decision had suggested the legal professional turned a "blind eye" to fraudulent activity. However, following the appeal, that finding has now been reversed. No further details regarding the identity of the solicitor or the specific nature of the case have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire roadwork delays drop following fines
stories.brief: New figures show a reduction in roadwork overruns across Cambridgeshire. The number of projects exceeding their planned duration has fallen by 42. This decrease follows the implementation of £424,000 in fines and charges issued to contractors. The data, reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, suggests that the financial penalties have been effective in encouraging works to be completed on schedule.

stories.headline: Long Sutton Neighbourhood Plan receives support
stories.brief: Long Sutton Parish Council has received backing for its neighbourhood plan. The move, reported by the Spalding South Holland News, marks a step forward in the local planning process for the area. No further details regarding the specific contents or the next stages of the plan have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Serious collision on the A142
stories.brief: A driver has been taken to hospital with serious injuries following a crash on the A142. Emergency services attended the scene of the incident. No further details regarding the circumstances of the collision or the current condition of the individual involved have been released at this time. Motorists are advised to remain aware of potential disruption in the area.

stories.headline: Robbie Savage comments on Peterborough United role
stories.brief: Robbie Savage has spoken about his position at Peterborough United. The former footballer has stated that he is prepared to prove his critics wrong in his new role at the club. No further details regarding his specific responsibilities or the nature of his appointment have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Plans submitted for final phase of East Cambridgeshire housing development
stories.brief: The Church Commissioners for England have submitted a planning application for the final stage of a major housing project in East Cambridgeshire. The proposal outlines the construction of 1,600 new homes as part of the community development.

stories.headline: East Cambridgeshire families encouraged to review household finances
stories.brief: Families living in East Cambridgeshire are being advised to review their current benefit entitlements and household bills. The recommendation comes as residents face ongoing increases in the cost of living. Local households are encouraged to check their financial circumstances to ensure they are receiving all the support available to them.

stories.headline: Peterborough parents patrol school crossing after safety concerns
stories.brief: Parents in Peterborough have begun patrolling a local school crossing themselves. The move follows a series of incidents at the site, prompting families to take action to ensure student safety. No further details regarding the specific nature of the incidents or the location of the crossing have been provided.

stories.headline: New bereavement centre opens in East Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A new facility for those experiencing bereavement has opened in East Cambridgeshire. The centre is situated by a lakeside, providing a dedicated space for support within the local community. Further details regarding the services offered at the site have not been provided.

stories.headline: Sponsorship deal provides boost for local football club
stories.brief: A football club in the region is reporting a renewed sense of pride following a new sponsorship agreement. The deal is expected to provide a significant boost to the club, according to reports from the Spalding South Holland News. Players have expressed positive sentiments regarding the partnership, which aims to support the team's ongoing development. Further details on the specific nature of the sponsorship have not been disclosed, but the club remains optimistic about the impact this investment will have on their future performance and local standing.

stories.headline: Historic steam train to visit Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A steam locomotive described as having a remarkable history is set to visit Cambridgeshire. Details regarding the specific train, the dates of its arrival, and its planned route through the county have not yet been confirmed. Residents and rail enthusiasts are advised to keep an eye on local updates for further information regarding the visit.

stories.headline: Arrangements underway to fill vacant councillor seats
stories.brief: Following the death of a local councillor, official procedures are now in place to fill the resulting vacancies. The South Holland News reports that arrangements are being made to appoint representatives to the seats left empty by the late official. Further details regarding the process or the specific wards affected have not yet been released. Residents are advised to monitor local council updates for information on how these positions will be filled.

stories.headline: BBC highlights historical significance of the Fens
stories.brief: The BBC has described the Fens as a location where the entirety of British prehistory is represented. The broadcaster highlighted the area's unique historical importance, suggesting that the landscape serves as a significant record of the nation's past.
